chapter: Silvers, Rampart Street and Army service
title: Army newspaper writing and first radio appearance
summary: He wrote for the company newspaper and once introduced a gospel group on Washington radio, then reflects on learning from mistakes.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: From combat. From combat. Yeah. And I got into special services, and it's true they had guys look like giants, taller than me, and big guys couldn't read or write, came out of Georgia, came out of Alabama, came out of Florida, they came from all over, whites and blacks, the whites had their problems too. See, because Bobby Burst, who was a sergeant at Camp Holabird, was crossed from me. He and I got to be good friends, of course, he was in one side of the camp, I'm on the other side of the camp, but we used to meet in the PX and sit down and talk together, nobody bothered us, but we would talk about what went on in the Army, and that's how I started writing, I started writing for the Army, at least for the company newspaper. Then I started, first time I got on the radio was in Washington, D.C., I went out there one Sunday, I introduced the gospel group, and that was my first venture into radio.

Yeah, in Washington, D.C. In D.C. Just one Sunday, I did it one time, they never called me back for anything, because the war was getting hot, and I had other duties at the camp, I couldn't get out like I wanted. The only time that I really wanted to get out, when I had some time, I was chasing the broads. I wasn't worried about being the one of the announcer then, or anything else, between my Army job, and having a good time every now and then, reading the Bible and a couple of books, that was me. But for me to just get out there to, no, but I had a good time doing what I was doing, I liked doing what I was doing. I made some mistakes in life that I'm sorry for, but I say this, that the mistakes that I made, they taught me very well. And what I'm saying, you have to live an experience, you cannot buy an experience, not at all. See, when I talk to my nieces, nephews, and my children, I tell them, tell my wife same thing, I'm smart, because I'm older than all of you. I'm head of the household, I'm the head guy around here, and I like being the head guy, and I'm still learning, but I'm learning for you guys, and you remember, you've got to keep me sharp. Just having fun with the family.
